page.content:
Replicants, rain-soaked Los Angeles, and the question of who counts as human.

How Blade Runner connects

  • Work: Blade Runner (1982) — The 1982 film is the central Blade Runner work.
  • Creator: Philip K. Dick — Dick's novel inspired the Blade Runner films.
  • Creator: Ridley Scott — Scott's 1982 film defined Blade Runner as a world.
  • Work: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? — Dick's novel is the source work of Blade Runner.
  • Work: Blade Runner 2049 — 2049 is the sequel that continues the city.

What is Blade Runner?

Blade Runner is Ridley Scott's 1982 adaptation of Philip K. Dick's Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?: Deckard hunts Nexus-6 replicants in Los Angeles 2019, Roy Batty wants more life, and the Voight-Kampff test tries to tell people from products. Denis Villeneuve's 2049 returns to that city with K and Joi.

Key threads lead to Blade Runner (1982), Philip K. Dick, Ridley Scott, Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? and Blade Runner 2049.
